questions.subtopic: 3C4 Risk and control monitoring techniques. Drift alerts nobody receives
questions.question: A cable maker's drift monitor on its AI quoting model still emails its alerts to a data scientist who left in March, and nobody else receives them. What should the risk analyst recommend as BEST?

options.A: Rebuild the quoting model on recent copper price data
options.B: Assign alerts to the model owner's role, with a response time
options.C: Point the alerts at the data scientist hired to fill the position
options.D: Review the drift limits that decide when alerts are sent

questions.key_concept: AI monitoring alerts go to the model owner's role with a response time, not to one person's mailbox, which goes unread once they leave.
questions.pre_read: Ask who, today, receives the monitor's alerts and has to act on them.
questions.correct_explanation: The alerts were addressed to one person, so they stopped reaching anyone when that person left. Assigning them to the model owner's role, with a response time, survives staff changes and puts the backlog and later alerts before someone accountable. Pointing them at the data scientist hired to fill the position is the runner-up: it restores delivery for now, but to one person outside the accountable owner, and fails again at the next departure.

wrong_explanations.A: Rebuilding the model acts before anyone has analyzed what the alerts show, and later alerts still go to a mailbox nobody reads.
wrong_explanations.C: The replacement restores delivery for now, but the alerts still go to one person rather than the accountable owner's role, and the next departure repeats the gap.
wrong_explanations.D: The limits may be set well; the gap is that no one in the business receives or acts on the alerts they raise.

tips: Eliminate: A rebuilds the model before anyone has read what the alerts show, and D tunes the limits when the gap is that nobody receives the alerts.
Final two: B beats C because the alerts stopped when the one person they went to left; a role the model owner answers for survives staff changes, while a replacement repeats the gap.
Exam cue: when an AI monitor's alerts still go to someone who has left, assign them to the model owner's role with a response time, so one departure cannot silence them.
questions.framework_ref: NIST AI 100-1 (AI RMF 1.0) MEASURE 2.4 (the functionality and behavior of the AI system are monitored when in production); NIST SP 800-137 Section 3.5 (Respond to Findings)

questions.subtopic: 3C6 Monitoring and reporting of emerging risks. Labels the board misreads
questions.question: A mortgage broker's board report labels emerging risks low, medium or high by the strength of their evidence, and directors have read the 'low' ones as minor. What should the risk analyst recommend as BEST?

options.A: A glossary of the labels, set alongside the board report
options.B: Share of emerging risks under each label, as a chart
options.C: A single loss estimate per emerging risk listed
options.D: Possible impact stated apart from its confidence level

questions.key_concept: Report an emerging risk's possible impact and the confidence behind it separately, so thin evidence is not read as low harm.
questions.pre_read: Ask what the report's labels actually measure, and what directors need to see besides.
questions.correct_explanation: The labels measure how strong the evidence is, yet directors read them as how serious the risks are, and the report shows nothing else. Stating each risk's possible impact separately from its confidence lets directors see both. A glossary of the labels is the runner-up: it would stop the misreading, but directors would still have no view of how much harm any emerging risk could do.

wrong_explanations.A: A glossary explains what the labels mean, but the report would still give directors no view of the harm each risk could cause.
wrong_explanations.B: A chart of how many risks carry each label still shows only the strength of the evidence, so the low ones still read as minor.
wrong_explanations.C: A single loss figure claims a precision the thin evidence cannot support; emerging risk is shown as a range with its confidence.

tips: Eliminate: B charts the same evidence labels, which still show nothing about harm, and C swaps ranges for single figures the evidence cannot support.
Final two: D beats A because a glossary corrects the misreading but still shows no harm; stating possible impact apart from confidence gives directors both.
Exam cue: report an emerging risk's possible impact and the confidence behind it as two separate things; one label that mixes them lets thin evidence read as low harm.
questions.framework_ref: NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 Section 2.3.1 (Risk Models: uncertainty can be communicated by giving ranges of values rather than single values); NIST IR 8286A Rev. 1 Section 2.2.5 (Recording Identified Risks: developing or emerging risks are yet to be fully defined but might disrupt enterprise objectives in the future)
